decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY capturing the geometry-first, black-and-white development mode and structural design basis; the material relationship is separately and fully owned by the source Requirement.
Deferring color influence while preserving champagne treatment as a long-term vision does not alter the accent's derivation from Hero V geometry or its requirement for shared material language.
The source decision governs the role and timing of metallic material treatment and does not change the deferred E and L letterform construction requirements.
The material-treatment decision does not change the deferred requirement that the full wordmark read as one cohesively kerned mark.
The second V remains derived from the Hero V and retains shared material language; postponing metallic treatment during geometry exploration does not alter those requirements.
The source decision does not change the second V's smaller, subordinate visual relationship to the Hero V.
